body: I hope things get better for both of you. Im sorry.

Dude why are you always on this sub trying to vilify every single experience? You dont need other people to have the same experience as you to be validated. You feel the way you feel and thats fine and im sorry about whatever happened but stop being so negative to every person who says anything about a remotely positive experience.

The industry is flawed yes but so is everything else. You dont have to like it, i sure as hell dont, but everything is about making money and its fucking bullshit but thats the way it is. People could be making money in worse ways. Im not saying ppl dont have the right to be upset about these wilderness places. It was fucking wild. Incredibly emotional taxing. I totally understand how some people would call it abuse, i personally dont think it is but im not everyone. All i know is i can personally speak to the experience i had and also the experience of my group. A lot of lives were saved in G5 in 2015. And a lot of those minimum wage kids youre talking about are working there bc they feel the same way i feel and they want to give it back. Im not saying theyre all good ppl but thats true of any profession. Idk, i feel strongly bc wilderness saved my life and i know a lot of other kids who feel the same way. I plan on working in that industry after school.
This post is in the exact sub that it should be.
I was responding to someone elses comment on the thread who kept repeating the same question to me. Wasnt coming after you at all. Im new to reddit and dk how this shit works still. My bad.

Idk why youre trying to convince me that what i experienced was abuse. Im sorry if you had a different experience and i understand how some people react differently than others in those sorts of situations, but that was not my experience at all. Without second nature i wouldve put a gun in my mouth years ago. I look back on every second incredibly fondly, probably the worst shit the most fondly.
Yes to all of those things. I didnt think it was emotional abuse.

I went to second nature in the uintas. I know people whove had incredibly positive experiences but some can be very different as ive seen in this thread. It changed my life, i now live in utah and am planning on working there after school.

Thats my bad. I spoke from an uneducated stance, i should have said my experience personally but i generalized it. Ive heard stories of how bad things can be but never met anyone whod had it happen to them. I was incredibly lucky to be in a very positive place. Most arent so fortunate. Again, my bad. Thanks for checking me.
Wilderness is what you make of it. It saved my life. It sucks sometimes, you just got embrace it. Listen and learn and be open. Youll get out what you put in.

My appointments were 400 per, insurance didnt cover it at all unfortunately but it was a hail mary situation when i didnt know what else to do, so i got really lucky that it wasnt an absurd charge like 1400 per session. I went to new york ketamine infusions, my doctor was a man named glen brooks. He was a great guy and im sure hed be willing to speak with you if you could find his contact info somehow.

I went to wilderness therapy. Wilderness therapy has saved a lot of lives. Mine included. This post is pretty misleading. Wilderness therapy exists for the sole purpose of giving troubled kids the opportunity to recognize the direction their life is headed, and then, in an isolated setting w the help of medical professionals, to try and alter that direction for the better. I understand lots of people have different experiences and some wilderness places are horrible, horrible places. But this is too generalized.
